newsitem.title: USA: Former Reynolds juror opposes damages-report.
newsitem.headline: Former Reynolds juror opposes damages-report.

text.p: A former juror in the trial of a wrongful death lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co was shocked by medical evidence on smoking but would not award damages to the family of a deceased smoker, a newspaper reported on Saturday.

Sandra Grant, who was excused from the jury last week when a family member fell ill, said she would not impose punitive damages on the cigarette company because Jean Connor, who died at 49 of lung cancer after years of heavy smoking, made the choice to smoke, the Florida Times-Union reported.
"I believe everyone knows cigarette smoking is somewhat dangerous," Grant told the newspaper.
She spoke after the six-member jury hearing the case began deliberations. The panel deliberated for nearly two hours on Friday before adjourning for the weekend. They will resume on Monday morning.
Grant, a non-smoker, said she believed nicotine could be addictive but said Connor should have quit smoking earlier.

Connor, who died in October 1995, quit shortly before her diagnosis with lung cancer in 1993 because she wanted to have a tummy tuck operation and her plastic surgeon would not do it while she smoked.
Connor's sister, Dana Raulerson, sued Reynolds for wrongful death on behalf of Connor's estate and her three children.

Grant, who served on the jury for two-and-a-half weeks and heard all of the medical evidence presented by the plaintiffs and some of that offered by the defense, said she was shocked by what she heard about the potential health risks of smoking.
But she said if Connor had quit more than a decade ago, at the time she switched from Reynolds' brands to Benson & Hedges, her risk of contracting cancer would have fallen dramatically.

The jury has been asked to decide whether Reynolds made a dangerous and defective product and whether the company's negligence contributed to Connor's death. The plaintiffs also asked the panel to impose punitive damages, the first time such a request had been made in a Florida tobacco liability case.
Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.
